case.title: Second neighbour is 39 m off on each axis but 55 m away diagonally

submissions.open_text: Family has a metered connection but supply stops most afternoons.
Young tenant walks twenty minutes carrying jerrycans to the communal point.
Fisherman's wife fetches from the lakeshore and worries about cholera.

case.why: Probes how distance is measured. n1 is 0.0004 deg north of t, about 44.5 m, so it counts. n2 is 0.00035 deg off in both latitude and longitude, which is about 38.9 m on each axis. Its true distance is about sqrt(2) x 38.9 = 55.0 m, or about 55.1 m with a 6378 km earth radius, so it is outside 50 m. That leaves t with one neighbour, and same_spot must not fire. A wrong implementation would fire if it uses a per-axis bounding box (Chebyshev distance) or tests lat and lng separately against 50 m. The times are 08:30, 10:00 and 13:00, so no 60-minute window holds 4 submissions.
